subject: Offsite kiosk update: signing, operator handshake, and evidentiary flow

Subject: Proposed kiosk handoff for Nexis Health IT offline bundle
Attachments: signed_manifest_v1.json (stub)

Hi Olga / team,

Following our call last week, Sierra Systems is proposing a kiosk-based handoff pattern for Nexis Health IT's air-gapped cluster updates. The idea is to minimize operator-hosted transfer steps and provide a single-operator UX that enforces verification before install. High level:

- Build and sign images in our secure build enclave.
- Produce a single signed bundle plus a detached manifest (attached).
- Ship sealed SSDs to the on-prem kiosk; on arrival, the kiosk performs signature verification using an offline root cert and then presents the operator with a one-button apply flow.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Is an HSM-signed artifact (detached manifest + signature) sufficient for your compliance team, or do you require additional notarization (eg. SigStore timestamping)?
2) What does the operator rotate/handshake flow need to look like from your runtime side (KV cache, docker image verification, attestation logs)?

We can provide a courier certificate and chain-of-custody manifest, but will need your checklist to ensure we meet Nexis' audit needs.

Thanks,
Allan
Allan McBride
Sierra Systems - Secure Delivery
allan.mcbride@sierra-sys.com

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed kiosk handoff for Nexis Health IT offline bundle

Allan, thanks for the summary and the manifest. Quick clarifications from Redwood before we scope details: 

- For Nexis we need end-to-end non-repudiation for every release. HSM signatures are good, but we also need a cryptographic timestamping/no-tamper proof (SigStore-style) recorded to our audit store. Because the kiosk is offline, the bundle needs an embedded signed timestamp or a notarization blob inside the manifest.

- Operator UX: the kiosk should NOT allow bypass. Operator presses a physical confirm button, the device runs verify -> local attest -> writes the install decision to the operator log, then applies. We will need the operator log format and a sample verification script (sha256 checks, signature verification, permitted-image list).

- Delivery: chain-of-custody proofs (courier cert) + signed manifest + operator instructions (we will provide a template). Please mark any fields in your manifest that are mutable after signing.

Attaching a template operator_key_instructions.txt that we use internally - this is the level of detail we expect. If you can produce a signed manifest that contains an embedded SigStore proof or timestamp field, that would satisfy our compliance team.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

All, adding a technical sketch so we have concrete ops steps to validate compliance: 

1) Build pipeline (Sierra) produces: image.tar.gz, tree-of-files, and detached manifest.json. Manifest contains: image_sha256, build_id, builder_key_id, timestamp.
2) Signing: Sierra signs manifest with their HSM key. They should also produce a SigStore-style rekor entry id or a signed timestamp blob which we can verify against our offline root. If rekor is impossible, include a signed timestamping service response embedded in manifest.
3) Bundle assembly: place image.tar.gz + manifest.json + signature -> encrypt at-rest with envelope keys (customer public key) -> write to sealed SSD.
4) Kiosk flow (on-prem):
   - Insert sealed SSD -> kiosk boots into verify mode.
   - Kiosk verifies signature chain using embedded offline root certs.
   - Kiosk checks manifest fields against allowlist (per configuration).
   - Kiosk prompts operator to press physical confirm -> kiosk runs pre-checks, writes operator decision to tamper-evident log.
   - Apply update via staged install; post-install attestations sent back when connectivity allowed.

Deliverables we need from Sierra: sample signed manifest, example signature verification tool (static binary or script), and courier chain-of-custody PDF. I attached a short operator_instructions template for your convenience.

Markus
Senior SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus, that helps. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

- We can include a SigStore Rekor entry id. Rekor is online, so we will embed the rekor entry proof within the manifest at build-time. That embedded proof is the artifact you can verify offline (it contains the timestamp + signed data).

- For sealed SSDs, Nexis prefers using tamper-evident hardware enclosures we supply; we can include a physical tracking barcode printed on the courier manifest.

- For the operator verification binary, we can provide an ELF static binary and a portable python script. Which do you prefer? For regulated sites they like mountable scripts with clear exit codes for automation.

We will attach the courier certificate and the initial signed_manifest_v1.json in our next message.

Allan

Subject: Re: Proposed kiosk handoff for Nexis Health IT offline bundle

Allan, quick security additions from our side before this is finalized: 

- Please ensure manifests include a rekor_proof field and a build_chain list (build system id, job id, artifact hashes). That allows us to map back to the build provenance even when offline.

- Operator log format: we require the following fields: operator_id, operator_key_fingerprint, action, bundle_id, pre_install_hash, install_result, timestamp, kiosk_serial, courier_barcode. Logs must be signed by the kiosk local key and stored in append-only fashion (we will provide a journal format).

- Key rotation: the kiosk should support on-site operator key replacement with dual-auth (operator + local admin). Rotation operations must generate a rotation event and a signed rotation_receipt.

- Auditing: we will require periodic ingest of logs to Redwood's secure audit store. Because sites are offline for long windows, the kiosk should support batching logs into an encrypted archive that can be uploaded when connectivity returns.

I'll draft a minimal attestation schema and share it to the Drive link in related_links. Once we have the signed_manifest and courier cert we can run an initial validation test in our lab.

Priyom
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
